irfan: Heads-up — nsys from the nightly load test shows a weird pattern: short bursts of host->device memcpy and stream synchronizations right after the vLLM wrapper calls into TRT. Looks like the scheduler hands off tiny requests and we pay a huge launcher/memcpy overhead. Uploaded perfetto: https://perfetto.redwood/internal/trace/abcd1234
sophie: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to replicate locally
ajay: used this: ```nsys profile -f true -o trt_vllm_night --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt python -m scripts/run_inference_loadtest.py --concurrency 64```
perf-bot: summary: gpu util 38%, cuda memcpy H2D spikes ~120us * 450 occurrences, avg kernel time 1.1ms but 60% of total time in enqueue/syncs (host side)
irfan: here's a clipped perfetto timeline: ```[HOST] wrapper::enqueue() -> nvtx_range(wrapper_enqueue) -> cudaMemcpyAsync(H2D, 512KB) -> cudaStreamSynchronize -> engine->execute() -> small kernels (matmul_1, attention_qk, softmax) x 28 -> cudaMemcpyAsync(D2H, 512KB)``` repeated per request
maria: interesting — our kvcache path is also doing conditional flush when seq_len < 8 because of an old eviction heuristic; could be causing extra memcpys for short conversations. log snippet: `KVCache::maybe_flush() - reason=short-seq, size=0.5MB`
sophie: so two things: (A) wrapper is issuing small, frequent memcpys and forcing syncs, (B) kernel launch overhead because kernels are tiny and launched separately. both add up.
ajay: i instrumented wrapper with NVTX and saw 2500 NVTX boundaries per second on that load. payloads were 128-512 tokens but often single-turn short requests. wrapper code: ```// pseudo
for (auto &chunk : chunks) {
  nvtxRangePush("enqueue_chunk");
  engine.enqueue(chunk); // issues H2D + kernel submissions
  nvtxRangePop();
}
```
irfan: test idea: switch to pinned host buffers + batch copies: allocatePinned(host_batch_buf, total_bytes); memcpy into single buffer, single cudaMemcpyAsync, then split on device. microbenchmark: `python infra/bench/pin_batch_mem.py --batch-size 64 --buf-size 4MB` showed 3x reduction in memcpy time for many small requests
maria: also we should tune the batching heuristic: current `batch_window_ms=10` flushes too aggressively for our bursty pattern. bump to 25ms resulted in 18% throughput improvement in a local replay of the issue.
sophie: could also explore kernel consolidation on the TRT side — some ops are launched as separate small kernels (elementwise ops). TRT plugin fusion helped in earlier runs. but need to measure if fusion increases peak memory usage
ajay: small datapoint: enabling continuous batching (window 25ms + max_batch 32) reduces NVTX boundaries by ~60% but increases tail latency for single-request cases. We should add a tiering policy: aggressive batching for non-SLA customers.
perf-bot: extra metrics dump: top host stacks during spikes -> wrapper::submit_batch -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> cudaStreamSynchronize -> runtime::wait_event
irfan: root cause hypothesis: vLLM wrapper currently does per-chunk enqueue+host copy, which is fine for large chunks but terrible for tiny requests. plus our KVCache evictions trigger D2H copies for small sequences. combined effect = memcpy storms + stream syncs.
maria: patches to try: 1) aggregate H2D into single batched copy in wrapper 2) fix KVCache eviction threshold to avoid flush for seq_len < 4 3) add NVTX at a finer granularity to see where stream syncs originate
sophie: action items: ajay -> prototype pinned-batch copy + NVTX ranges (end of day), irfan -> run perfetto + nsys on patched build with quantization off (to keep kernels comparable), maria -> open bug for kvcache-eviction and add unit test
ajay: small WIP snippet for aggregated copy: ```// allocate once
void* host_pinned = cudaHostAlloc(total_bytes, cudaHostAllocDefault);
// populate
memcpy(host_pinned + offset, src, len);
// single async copy
cudaMemcpyAsync(dev_buf, host_pinned, total_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream);
```
irfan: also add a perf regression gate: if memcpy H2D spikes > 50% of request time in nsys baseline vs PR, fail perf run. can write a simple parser to check `nsys stats` output
maria: noted. i'll create the perf-checker job in CI (low priority queue)
